_The Walking Dead_ was renewed by AMC for a 16-episode eighth season on October 16, 2016.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-ew_s8-4) Production began on April 25, 2017, in Atlanta, Georgia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-5) On July 12, 2017, production was shut down after stuntman John Bernecker was killed, after falling more than 20 feet onto a concrete floor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-6) Production resumed on July 17.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-7) The season premiere, which also serves as the series' milestone 100th episode, was directed by executive producer Greg Nicotero.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Director801-8)

In November 2017, it was announced that Lennie James who portrays Morgan Jones, would be leaving _The Walking Dead_ after the conclusion of this season, and would join the cast of the spin-off series _Fear the Walking Dead_ for its fourth season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-9) The eighth season also features the departures of series regulars Chandler Riggs (Carl Grimes), Steven Ogg (Simon), and Austin Amelio (Dwight). Riggs' final episode is the mid-season premiere where his character is killed off, which is a deviation from the comic book, where his character is still alive. His death received negative reactions from critics and fans.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-10) Ogg's final episode is the penultimate episode of the season, where his character is killed by Negan.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-11) Amelio departed the series after the season finale, and in January 2019, it was confirmed he would join the cast of _Fear the Walking Dead_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-12)
The first trailer for the season was released on July 21, 2017 at San Diego Comic-Con. The second trailer was released on February 1, 2018 for the second part of the season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-29)
On March 15, 2018, it was announced that the season finale and the fourth season premiere of _Fear the Walking Dead_ would be screened at AMC, Regal, and Cinemark theaters across the United States on April 15, the same day as the TV airing, for "Survival Sunday: _The Walking Dead_&_Fear the Walking Dead_". The episodes marked the first crossover between the two series. The cinema screening also included an extra half-hour of exclusive bonus content.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Cinema-30)

The eighth season of _The Walking Dead_ received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, the season holds a score of 65% with an average rating of 6.65 out of 10 based on 447 reviews. The site's critical consensus reads: "_The Walking Dead_'s eighth season energizes its characters with some much-needed angst and action, though it's still occasionally choppy and lacking forward-moving plot progression."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-RT_S8-31)

For the 44th Saturn Awards, the eighth season of _The Walking Dead_ received seven nominations, winning two. It won Best Horror Television Series and Best Performance by a Younger Actor in a Television Series (Chandler Riggs).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-S44-1) The nominations were for Best Actor on Television (Andrew Lincoln), Best Supporting Actor on Television (Khary Payton), Best Supporting Actress on Television (Danai Gurira and Melissa McBride), and Best Guest Starring Role on Television (Jeffrey Dean Morgan).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-32)

_The Walking Dead_ was renewed by AMC for a 16-episode eighth season on October 16, 2016.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-ew_s8-4) Production began on April 25, 2017, in Atlanta, Georgia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-5) On July 12, 2017, production was shut down after stuntman John Bernecker was killed, after falling more than 20 feet onto a concrete floor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-6) Production resumed on July 17.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-7) The season premiere, which also serves as the series' milestone 100th episode, was directed by executive producer Greg Nicotero.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Director801-8)

In November 2017, it was announced that Lennie James who portrays Morgan Jones, would be leaving _The Walking Dead_ after the conclusion of this season, and would join the cast of the spin-off series _Fear the Walking Dead_ for its fourth season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-9) The eighth season also features the departures of series regulars Chandler Riggs (Carl Grimes), Steven Ogg (Simon), and Austin Amelio (Dwight). Riggs' final episode is the mid-season premiere where his character is killed off, which is a deviation from the comic book, where his character is still alive. His death received negative reactions from critics and fans.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-10) Ogg's final episode is the penultimate episode of the season, where his character is killed by Negan.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-11) Amelio departed the series after the season finale, and in January 2019, it was confirmed he would join the cast of _Fear the Walking Dead_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-12)
The first trailer for the season was released on July 21, 2017 at San Diego Comic-Con. The second trailer was released on February 1, 2018 for the second part of the season.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-29)
On March 15, 2018, it was announced that the season finale and the fourth season premiere of _Fear the Walking Dead_ would be screened at AMC, Regal, and Cinemark theaters across the United States on April 15, the same day as the TV airing, for "Survival Sunday: _The Walking Dead_&_Fear the Walking Dead_". The episodes marked the first crossover between the two series. The cinema screening also included an extra half-hour of exclusive bonus content.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-Cinema-30)

The eighth season of _The Walking Dead_ received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, the season holds a score of 65% with an average rating of 6.65 out of 10 based on 447 reviews. The site's critical consensus reads: "_The Walking Dead_'s eighth season energizes its characters with some much-needed angst and action, though it's still occasionally choppy and lacking forward-moving plot progression."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-RT_S8-31)

For the 44th Saturn Awards, the eighth season of _The Walking Dead_ received seven nominations, winning two. It won Best Horror Television Series and Best Performance by a Younger Actor in a Television Series (Chandler Riggs).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-S44-1) The nominations were for Best Actor on Television (Andrew Lincoln), Best Supporting Actor on Television (Khary Payton), Best Supporting Actress on Television (Danai Gurira and Melissa McBride), and Best Guest Starring Role on Television (Jeffrey Dean Morgan).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-32)
The first half of the season was nominated for Outstanding Performance by a Stunt Ensemble in a Television Series at the 24th Screen Actors Guild Awards.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_season_8#cite_note-33)

Going from north to south, the northernmost portion of Fulton County, encompassing Milton and northern Alpharetta, is located in the Etowah River sub-basin of the ACT River Basin (Alabama-Coosa-Tallapoosa River Basin). Fulton County is a no-brainer for anyone looking to experience the heart of Georgia. It’s home to most of Atlanta, the state’s capital and largest city. From the bustling streets of Midtown to the quiet suburbs of Alpharetta, Fulton has diverse living options.
The county boasts world-class attractions like the Georgia Aquarium and the High Museum of Art. Atlanta’s pro sports teams, including the Braves and Falcons, call Fulton home. The county’s economy is a powerhouse, with major corporations headquartered here.
Despite its urban core, Fulton has plenty of green spaces, including the popular Atlanta BeltLine. The county’s history is rich, from Civil War sites to Civil Rights landmarks. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the world’s busiest, sits partly in Fulton. Fulton County showcases the many faces of modern Georgia with its southern tip and its northern suburbs.
